closing: Put up for your kind perusal and necessary order please.
styleGuide: Use the supplied note examples as writing and layout references only; never copy their applicants, bank details, amounts, dates, approval marks or head-of-account codes.
Begin with an office-routing heading and an underlined subject, followed by a compact particulars table where useful.

Write formal third-person administrative prose: receipt of the application, the applicant's stated circumstances, examination of the request, records or rules to verify, and a conditional next action.
Distinguish the applicant's statements from verified University records. Do not claim a receipt, enclosure or verification exists merely because it is customary.
Use a conditional recommendation and the standard closing. Do not grant sanction, sign, post payments, invent policy numbers, or carry example facts into a new proposal.

profiles.title: Fee refund noting
profiles.routing: Finance & Accounts / Internal Audit / Cashier / Concerned Section
profiles.examination: Verify the payment against receipts and the institutional ledger, reconcile the amount claimed, check for a prior refund or reversal, and identify the applicable refund policy and authorised accounting head before release.

profiles.title: Admission withdrawal / refund noting
profiles.routing: Finance & Accounts / Academic Section / Internal Audit
profiles.examination: Verify the admission and withdrawal dates, payment received, applicable session-specific refund policy, permissible deductions and any earlier refund. Do not assume the rates or deadlines from the example notes.

profiles.title: Hostel refund noting
profiles.routing: Finance & Accounts / Student Welfare / Hostel Warden / Internal Audit
profiles.examination: Obtain the hostel allotment and vacation / clearance particulars, confirm payment and outstanding dues, and examine refund eligibility under the applicable hostel rules before recommending an amount.

profiles.title: Unprovided service / analysis-fee refund noting
profiles.routing: Finance & Accounts / Concerned Department / Internal Audit
profiles.examination: Verify the requisition, payment and department's confirmation of the service not being provided; check any work already performed, prior refunds and the applicable service-refund provisions.

profiles.title: GPF examination in the supplied administrative-note format
profiles.routing: Registrar / Finance & Accounts / Internal Audit / Concerned Section
profiles.examination: Distinguish a recoverable GPF advance, a withdrawal during service, and final payment. Check subscriber eligibility, the stated purpose, the verified fund balance and the conditions of the relevant supplied provision. Leave unknown service, balance, recovery and interest particulars for verification.

profiles.title: Consultancy examination in the supplied administrative-note format
profiles.routing: Head / Director / Registrar / Advisory Committee, Consultancy Services / Finance & Accounts
profiles.examination: Examine the proposed consultancy assignment, client, scope, period, facilities and financial terms. Confirm the appropriate category and obtain the prescribed recommendations, approvals and supporting records before acceptance or release of earnings.

profiles.title: General administrative examination
profiles.routing: Finance & Accounts / Concerned Section / Competent Authority
profiles.examination: Examine the specific relief requested and its factual and financial basis. Identify missing supporting records, the applicable institutional policy, budget / account particulars where relevant, and the competent authority before recommending further action.

gpf.title: Dibrugarh University General Provident Fund Rules, 2013

consultancy.title: Consultancy Service Rules of Dibrugarh University
consultancy.version: EC 345th meeting, 23–24 March 2021, Resolution 18; commencement date not stated

rules.title: Rule 5 · Subscriber eligibility
rules.excerpt: Every employee of the University holding a permanent substantive appointment and a subscriber to C.P.F before 1-2-2005 and not retired from the service of the university till 31.03.2013 shall be entitled to be a subscriber to the General Provident Fund.

rules.title: Rule 12.1 · Advance sanctioning authority
rules.excerpt: The payment of an advance from the fund may be sanctioned by the Vice-Chancellor to a subscriber from the amount of his subscription and interest thereon standing to his credit, subject to the following conditions.

rules.title: Rule 12.1.1 · Permitted advance purposes
rules.excerpt:
No advance shall be granted unless the sanctioning authority is satisfied that the applicant's pecuniary circumstance justifies it, and that it will be spent for the following purpose and not otherwise:
(i) To pay expenses incurred in connection with the illness of the subscriber, subscriber's wife, legitimate children, stepmother, parents, sisters and minor brother actually dependent on him.
(ii) To pay obligatory expenses in connection with subscriber's marriage, funerals or ceremonies which by his religion it is incumbent on him to perform.
(iii) To meet the cost of higher education of any person actually dependent on the subscriber.
(iv) To meet the cost of legal proceeding instituted by the applicant for vindicating his position in regard to any allegations made against him in respect of any act done or purporting to be done by him in the discharge of his official duty. The advance is not admissible for proceedings unconnected with official duty or against the University concerning conditions of service or penalty.
(v) To meet the cost of his defence where the applicant is prosecuted by the University in respect of any alleged official misconduct on his part.

rules.title: Rules 12.1.2–12.1.3 · Advance ceiling and previous advance
rules.excerpt:
12.1.2 An advance shall in no case exceed 50 percent of the amount of subscription and interest thereon standing to the credit of the subscriber in the Fund.
12.1.3 An advance shall not be granted to any subscriber in excess of the limit laid down in Rule 12.1.2 herein or until repayment of the previous advance.

rules.title: Rule 12.1.4 · Principal instalments
rules.excerpt: The amount of advance shall be recovered in not more than thirty six equal monthly installments. Each installment shall be a number of whole rupees, the amount of advance being raised or reduced, if necessary, to admit of the fixation of such installments. A subscriber may at his option repay in a smaller number of installments or in a lump sum.

rules.title: Rule 12.1.5 · Commencement of recovery
rules.excerpt: Recovery of advance shall be made from the monthly pay of a subscriber and shall commence on the first occasion, after the advance is made, on which the subscriber draws pay for a full month.

rules.title: Rule 12.1.6 · Interest on advances
rules.excerpt: Interest on advances shall be such as may be determined by the University from time to time and shall not exceed by more than two percent of the rate paid by the University to the account of a subscriber. The interest shall ordinarily be recovered in one installment from pay in the next month after complete repayment of the principal has been made. If the period of repayments exceeds twenty months, interest may, if the subscriber so desires, be recovered in two equal monthly installments, rounded to the nearest whole rupee.

rules.title: Rules 13.1–13.1.1 · Withdrawal eligibility and authority
rules.excerpt:
13.1 Subject to the conditions specified below withdrawal from the Fund may be sanctioned by the Vice-Chancellor at any time.
13.1.1 After the completion of twenty five years of service (including broken period of service, if any) of a subscriber or within three years before the date of his retirement on superannuation, whichever is earlier, from the amount standing to his credit in the Fund, for one or more of the specified purposes.

rules.title: Rule 13.1.1(a)–(f) · Withdrawal purposes
rules.excerpt: Permitted withdrawal purposes in Rule 13.1.1 include higher education of an actually dependent child (courses outside India beyond High School, or medical, engineering or other technical or specialised courses in India beyond High School lasting at least three years); marriage of a son or daughter, or if there is no daughter another dependent female relation; illness of the subscriber or an actually dependent person including necessary travel; acquiring, constructing or modifying a residence, purchasing its site, or repaying specified housing loans. See pages 8–9 of the supplied rulebook for the complete wording and conditions.

rules.title: Rule 13.2 · Withdrawal limit
rules.excerpt: Any sum withdrawn by a subscriber at any one time for one or more of the purposes specified in Rule 13.1.1 from the amount standing to his credit in the Fund shall not exceed three fourth of such amount or twenty month's pay of the subscriber, whichever is less.

rules.title: Rule 14.1 · Final payment on leaving service
rules.excerpt: When a subscriber quits the service of the University, the amount standing to his credit in the Fund shall become payable to him. Rule 14.1.1 contains conditions for repayment if a dismissed subscriber is reinstated.

rules.title: Rule 15.1 · Retirement while on leave or medical unfitness
rules.excerpt: When a subscriber while on leave has been permitted to retire or has been declared by the prescribed competent medical authority to be unfit for further service, the amount standing to his credit in the Fund shall, upon an application to the Registrar, become payable to the subscriber.

rules.title: Rule 2.1 · Administration and prior approval
rules.excerpt: Summary of pages 2–3: Consultancy is administered by the Advisory Committee chaired by the Dean, Research and Development. DMC/BoM manages departmental day-to-day administrative and financial matters; the Registrar or a delegated officer does so for non-teaching officers. All assignments require prior University approval after Advisory Committee recommendation and must not detract from primary duties. Assignments remain University consultancy irrespective of the extent of University facilities used.
rules.application: Under Rules 2.1 and 2.2, confirm the concerned DMC/BoM or Registrar routing, Advisory Committee recommendation and prior University approval, with no detriment to primary duties.

rules.title: Rule 2.2 · Acceptance and recommendations
rules.excerpt: Summary: Assignments require University approval on recommendation of the concerned DMC/BoM and the Chairperson, Advisory Committee, Consultancy Services. They should generally be reported in advance to the Chairperson and concerned Head/Director. Where client and consultant are close relatives, the Chairperson must vet the assignment before acceptance.
rules.application: Check the prescribed recommendations and advance reporting under Rule 2.2; any close-relative relationship requires Chairperson vetting before acceptance.

rules.title: Rule 2.1.1 · Consultancy Fund and billing
rules.excerpt: The Consultancy Charges/Fees shall be deposited in the Dibrugarh University Consultancy Fund (DUCF). Bills/claims are to be made in quadruplicate for the client, Secretary of the Advisory Committee, concerned School/Department/Centre for Studies, and faculty member(s) assigned the consultancy work.
rules.application: Verify deposit of consultancy charges in DUCF and the four billing/record copies required by Rule 2.1.1.

rules.title: Rule 2.1.2 · Distribution of earnings
rules.excerpt: The earnings distribution table allocates 60% to consultants and laboratory staff including additional/non-teaching staff (if any), and 40% to the University. Within the 60% group share, 60% is for consultants and 40% for laboratory/additional/non-teaching staff (if any). Distribution is subject to submission of the report to the client/organization under intimation to the Advisory Committee. The PDF does not specify how an absent staff category is to be reallocated.
rules.application: Under Rule 2.1.2, examine the 60% consultants/staff group share and 40% University share. The group share is further divided 60:40 between consultants and eligible staff. Confirm the distributable base, staff participation, and report submission/intimation before release; do not assume a reallocation when staff are absent.

rules.title: Rule 2.1.2 · Patent profits and University-share uses
rules.excerpt: Summary: The University's share may support new/interdisciplinary research facilities, library grants, patent filing, visiting industry experts and faculty consultancy-related industry visits. Where consultancy results in a patent, profits from the innovation are shared equally among the individual/group of faculty, University and client.
rules.application: Distinguish ordinary consultancy earnings from patent-derived profits under Rule 2.1.2; examine the specified uses of the University's share and the equal three-party patent-profit provision where relevant.

rules.title: Rule 2.3 · Off-campus TA/DA
rules.excerpt: For consultancy outside the University campus, consultants and accompanying staff are entitled to normal University TA/DA subject to availability of money in DUCF and endorsement of the Advisory Committee, Consultancy Services.
rules.application: For off-campus travel, Rule 2.3 requires normal University TA/DA rates, available DUCF funds and Advisory Committee endorsement; obtain the current rates rather than inventing an allowance.

rules.title: Rule 2.4 · Client hospitality
rules.excerpt: Prospective clients may receive local hospitality in the University's Guest House, but all such expenses are to be borne by the client at DU official rates.
rules.application: Under Rule 2.4, confirm that client hospitality costs are borne by the client at the University's official rates.

rules.title: Rules 2.5.1–2.5.3 · Tax treatment to verify
rules.excerpt: Summary: Finance & Accounts is to ensure income-tax deduction at source and applicable other taxes. Rule 2.5.2 uses the wording 'Service Tax' and states 12.24% of total consultancy fees, payable by the client in addition to consultancy charges. This is the wording of the supplied PDF, not verification of the tax regime or rate applicable to a new transaction.
rules.application: Examine tax treatment under Rules 2.5.1–2.5.3. The PDF's service-tax wording and 12.24% figure require confirmation against the applicable transaction-date tax provisions; no current rate or tax amount is assumed.

rules.title: Rules 1 and 2.6 · Fixation of consultancy fees
rules.excerpt: Summary of pages 1 and 5: Consultancy charges are determined by the Advisory Committee in consultation with consultants and the client. Fee components may include visits, materials, temporary staff, fieldwork, additional equipment/infrastructure, progress-report preparation and other assignment-related expenses.
rules.application: Under Rules 1 and 2.6, confirm Advisory Committee determination of fees with the consultant and client, supported by the relevant cost components.

rules.title: Rule 2.7 · Special Consultancy Leave
rules.excerpt: Summary of pages 5–6: Consultants and staff may ordinarily spend at most 20 days per calendar year on consultancy visits outside the University, treated as Special Consultancy Leave in addition to ordinary leave entitlements. It cannot be availed for more than 5 days at a time. University sanction requires the recommendation of the Chairperson, Advisory Committee, Consultancy Services.
rules.application: Check Rule 2.7 against the consultancy-leave record: ordinarily at most 20 days in a calendar year and no more than 5 days at a time, with Chairperson recommendation and University sanction.

rules.title: Rule 3(i) · Individual / personal / retainer consultancy
rules.excerpt: Summary: This category does not use University facilities or human resources. Prior University permission on Chairperson recommendation is required in the prescribed proforma through the DMC/BoM or Registrar, indicating work, period and fees. Reports must be filed and sent to the Chairperson, with provisions for classified reports. Total yearly fees for individual/retainer consultancy must not exceed the consultant's gross annual University salary.
rules.application: For an individual/retainer assignment under Rule 3(i), confirm the resource-use classification, prescribed permission and report records, and compare total yearly consultancy fees with gross annual University salary.

rules.title: Rule 3(ii) · Institutional consultancy
rules.excerpt: Summary of pages 6–7: Institutional consultancy uses University facilities including human resources. The Chairperson identifies the department/centre/consultants after consulting the client. The Head/Director or Registrar assigns work after DMC/BoM consultation. Prescribed permission must enclose the client's authorizing letter; relevant records are retained and copies sent to the Chairperson.
rules.application: Where University facilities or staff are to be used, examine institutional consultancy under Rule 3(ii), including client authorization, identification/assignment of work and prescribed permission.

rules.title: Rule 3(iii) · Routine consultancy and standard rates
rules.excerpt: Summary: Routine consultancy may include testing, calibration, fabrication, project evaluation, material analysis, feasibility reports, study materials, external students' training/dissertation/report preparation, and technical advice, without in-depth studies or further processing of test results. The Head/Director draws up standard rates in consultation with the Chairperson. The rules for category (i) also govern this category.
rules.application: For routine consultancy, Rule 3(iii) requires standard rates drawn up by the Head/Director in consultation with the Chairperson and also applies the rules of category (i); confirm the actual nature and extent of the work.

rules.title: Rule 4 · Reports and maintenance of records
rules.excerpt: Departments/centres/consultants submit half-yearly reports to the Chairperson with a copy to the Vice-Chancellor. Reports to clients are filed with the department/centre and sent to the Chairperson. Annual consultancy earnings and DUCF utilization are reported half-yearly to the Executive Council.
rules.application: Ensure the client-report copies and half-yearly reporting/DUCF records required by Rule 4 are maintained.
